name: i2pd
desc: Full-featured C++ implementation of I2P client
why: A full I2P router is a genuine door into an anonymous overlay network most people have never run.

brief.what_it_is: i2pd (I2P Daemon) is a full-featured C++ implementation of an I2P client, the software that joins and uses the I2P anonymous network. Per the README it is used for anonymous peer-to-peer applications such as filesharing and cryptocurrencies, and for anonymous client-server applications such as websites, instant messengers and chat servers. The README lists its features as a distributed anonymous networking framework, end-to-end encrypted communications, a small footprint with simple dependencies, and a rich set of APIs for developers of secure applications. The fetched pages do not spell out the inputs and outputs in detail beyond this.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames the project as building a network that lets people communicate and share information without restrictions, free from censorship and privacy violations. The README says I2P is a universal anonymous network layer in which participants do not reveal their real IP addresses.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internal mechanism. It says all communications over I2P are anonymous and end-to-end encrypted, and that participants do not reveal their real IP addresses. The linked specifications at geti2p.net/spec and the documentation at i2pd.readthedocs.io were not fetched, so the routing details are unverified.
brief.install_notes: The README says the easiest route is precompiled packages and binaries from the GitHub releases page, and points to the documentation for install details. Build-from-source guides exist for unix, windows, iOS and android in the docs. Packaging channels named in the README include Docker (purplei2p/i2pd on Docker Hub), Snap, and distro packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, CentOS, Mageia, Alpine, Arch, openSUSE, Gentoo and FreeBSD. Configuration is via a config file, with an example at contrib/i2pd.conf in the repo, and the run guide is in the user-guide docs. The Android app and the Qt GUI live in separate repositories (i2pd-android and i2pd-qt), and the README mentions a third-party macOS GUI (gui-i2pd). I did not see first-run steps or any account requirement in the fetched text.
brief.standout: It is a complete I2P router written in C++ with a small footprint and few dependencies, and it runs on a wide range of platforms, including as a Docker image and Snap. The README also mentions a Qt GUI and an Android app as separate projects, so the daemon can run headless. The homepage's pitch is that running a node 24/7 helps protect civil rights online.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the fetched pages show. The README carries an active GitHub latest-release badge, CI build badges for Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD and Docker, Crowdin localization, and packaging-status badges. I did not see a release date or last-commit date in the fetched text, so recency is unverified.
brief.caveats: The README gives no explicit platform limit beyond the supported-systems list. The licence is BSD 3-clause, per the README. Building from source requires following the separate docs for each OS. The README includes a 'No LLM/AI policy': no LLM or AI generated code for pull requests and no LLM or AI generated text for issues. The homepage is only partly translated in the fetched content and the donation addresses are crypto wallets. The brew description and the scout note are the only sources for the 'genuine door' framing, and the README itself does not make that claim.
quotes: i2pd (I2P Daemon) is a full-featured C++ implementation of I2P client.
I2P (Invisible Internet Protocol) is a universal anonymous network layer.
Small footprint, simple dependencies, fast performance
Free from censorship. Free from privacy violations.
